We start Module 4 on Evaluation Metrics for Classification.

Once you have a classification model, you need to know how well it performs. Accuracy alone can be misleading, especially when classes are imbalanced. With the right metrics, you can compare models and report performance you can trust.

We cover:

- Accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score
- Confusion matrices
- ROC curves and AUC
- Cross-validation
- Comparing against a dummy baseline

Materials:
https://github.com/DataTalksClub/machine-learning-zoomcamp/tree/main/04-evaluation

We start Module 6 on Decision Trees and Ensemble Learning.

Linear models are a good start, but tree-based models often work better on tabular data. In this module, we build a credit risk scoring model and combine many trees into stronger models.

We cover:

- How we train decision trees
- Random forests
- Gradient boosting with XGBoost
- Hyperparameter tuning
- Feature importance
- Selecting the best model

Materials:
https://github.com/DataTalksClub/machine-learning-zoomcamp/tree/main/06-trees

Homework 6 applies tree-based models to the 2026 Car Fuel Efficiency dataset.

actions.text:
We start the midterm project.

For the next two weeks, you apply everything from Modules 1 to 6 to a problem of your choice. You pick a dataset, train and evaluate a model, and deploy it as a web service.

The project should include:

- A problem description and how the model will be used
- Data preparation and EDA with feature importance analysis
- Several trained and tuned models, and the one you selected
- A training script and a prediction service exported from the notebook
- Dependency and environment files, and a Dockerfile
- A deployed model, or a video or screenshot of the running service

Use a new public dataset. Datasets from the lectures and homework don't count.

Project guidelines:
https://github.com/DataTalksClub/machine-learning-zoomcamp/tree/main/projects
